evals.prompt: I want to add rate limiting to our REST API. Right now we have a Node.js/Express app with no rate limiting at all, and we're getting hammered by some clients making thousands of requests per minute. I need to limit each API key to 1000 requests per hour, return proper 429 errors, and have a way to check current usage. Can you create the planning docs for this?
evals.expected_output: HLD covering architecture of rate limiting middleware, LLD with Redis/in-memory store design, token bucket or sliding window algorithm, EARS requirements with FR/PR/SR numbered items, and an implementation plan with phased tasks

assertions.text: Output contains all four required sections: HLD, LLD, EARS requirements plan, and Implementation Plan
EARS section contains numbered requirements (e.g. FR-1, PR-1, SR-1) using proper EARS syntax templates (WHEN/WHILE/IF THEN/The system shall)
Implementation Plan includes a phased checklist with actionable tasks (starting with verbs like Create, Implement, Write, Add)
Documents address the specific requirements: 1000 req/hour limit, 429 error responses, and a usage-check mechanism
LLD includes discussion of rate-limiting algorithm (e.g. sliding window, token bucket, fixed window) with data structure details
Implementation Plan includes a risk assessment section with at least 2 risks identified

evals.prompt: We need to add real-time notifications to our web app. Users should get notified when someone comments on their post, likes their content, or sends them a direct message. We're using a Python/Django backend and React frontend. The notifications should appear as a bell icon with a badge count. Help me plan this out end-to-end.
evals.expected_output: HLD with WebSocket or SSE architecture decision, LLD with notification data model and delivery mechanism, EARS requirements covering notification triggers and delivery guarantees, implementation plan broken into phases

assertions.text: Output contains all four required sections: HLD, LLD, EARS requirements plan, and Implementation Plan
EARS section contains numbered requirements using proper EARS syntax (WHEN/WHILE/IF THEN/The system shall)
HLD discusses the real-time delivery mechanism (WebSocket, SSE, or long-polling) with rationale for the choice
Documents cover all three notification trigger types mentioned: comment on post, like, and direct message
LLD includes a notification data model/schema (fields like user_id, type, content, read_at, created_at etc.)
Implementation Plan is broken into at least 3 distinct phases with tasks in each

evals.prompt: I need to add an export to CSV feature for our analytics dashboard. Users have been asking for this for months. They should be able to select a date range, pick which metrics they want exported, and download a CSV file. We have a lot of data — some exports could have millions of rows — so it needs to handle large exports gracefully, probably with async processing and an email link when ready.
evals.expected_output: HLD with async job queue architecture, LLD with job model, CSV generation logic, email delivery, EARS requirements including async behavior and error handling, phased implementation plan with tasks

assertions.text: Output contains all four required sections: HLD, LLD, EARS requirements plan, and Implementation Plan
EARS section contains numbered requirements using proper EARS syntax (WHEN/WHILE/IF THEN/The system shall)
HLD or LLD addresses the async job/queue architecture for handling large exports (not synchronous download)
Documents address the large data concern (millions of rows) with specific strategies like streaming, chunking, or background jobs
Implementation plan or LLD covers email notification/link delivery when the export is ready
Implementation Plan includes a 'Definition of Done' section with completion criteria checklist
